text:
It's a real shame that I have to give you own star. If I  could I'd give you a zero .
Today I went to the queen's street mall McDonald's again for some dumb reason.
The McDonald's at queen st brisbane is not only always dirty, rubbish overflowing out of the bins, but also the service and the food and attitude is completely unacceptable.
Firstly, I got a burger served to me with a large hole in the meat.
I told the lady that the burger isn't very appetising and showed her and she said oh ok is it the hole? Did you want another one? No apology. Then I just took the new burger quietly and said ok mistakes happen but then I ordered an ice-cream with flake. I ordered it to be delivered to the table as wasn't feeling well. I needed to rest so I ordered it to the table.
Time passed and noone was coming so I had no choice to get up and ask.
The ice cream had been sitting on the bench melting because she was too lazy to walk to my table which wasn't far from the front counter.
She gave me a small cup with an ice-cream upside down melted and the flake was buried inside it somewhere. The icecream was a mess and I told her but she just  couldn't be bothered. I have been giving feedback before and I don't know why I was stupid to go back and today was my last day.
They have lazy staff with a bad attitude , no customer service skills, dirty premises and poor attention to detail with food preparation and lack of hygiene. Today going to the queen st  McDonald's was a stressful and disappointing experience for the last time. you could not pay me to go back there.
I'm completely done with McDonalds and I can honestly say that this McDonald's in Brisbane is an embarrassment to the McDonald's company. Good riddance
author: Dionisia

text:
Today is my birthday, and I came to dine with my friends. When I returned from the restroom, I discovered that my order was missing both the ice cream and the drink. I went to the counter to report the issue. After returning to my seat and opening my burger, I found that the Chicken Mac I ordered had been replaced with a beef burger. I do not eat beef, so I immediately went back to the counter. I showed the staff my receipt and the opened burger, clearly explaining that I ordered a Chicken Mac and was given a beef burger.

What happened next was absolutely unacceptable. The staff member looked directly at the beef burger in my hand and insisted, “This is the chicken burger.” I had to hold back my anger and told her again, “This is a beef burger.” It is unbelievable that an employee at McDonald’s cannot tell the difference between a fried chicken patty and a beef patty.

It only became even more ridiculous when another employee walked by and the staff member stopped her to ask, while pointing at my burger, “Is this a chicken burger?” The other employee immediately replied, “That’s a beef burger,” and replaced it with the correct order. This clearly shows that the initial staff member had no idea what she was talking about.

This is a serious issue with employee training. If she wasn’t sure, she should have confirmed with another staff member instead of confidently giving wrong information. And frankly, it is shocking that McDonald’s employees would need to be reminded of something as basic as distinguishing chicken from beef. I never expected that I would have to point out such a fundamental mistake. It completely ruined my birthday dining experience.
author: Leia Huang

text: The food at this McDonald’s was fresh and my order came out really quickly, with nothing missing, which I appreciated. Ordering was easy and fast, so that part of the experience was great. My drink and ice cream weren’t filled up all the way, and they also weren’t using the correct cups for frozen drinks, which was a bit disappointing. The tables in the dining area were quite dirty and could use more regular cleaning. On a positive note, the bins weren’t overflowing as they were being changed regularly, and the napkin dispensers around the store were well stocked, which is really convenient as you don’t have to ask for more. Finding the toilets was a bit confusing since there aren’t any clear signs, and while the toilets themselves were somewhat clean, the mirrors were noticeably dirty. Overall, the food and speed of service were good, but the cleanliness and attention to detail could definitely be improved.
author: Ashlee Aird

text:
I've been to many, many McDonalds on 4 different continents in my 66 years. This one was terrible. The worst.

Initially tried ordering at the kiosk and it kicked me out twice. Stood in line and was served. Paid but did not get a receipt but saw the charge go through my credit card. Waited for a bit then said to the lady that served me that I did not get a number or receipt. She said I hadn't paid. I said yes I had and she said I hadn't. At that point I was pretty frustrated so just paid again under protest. A few minutes later she called me over and said I had paid and processed a refund. No apology. A refund did finally come through my credit card, several days after the two charges.

I know people make mistakes and I know people have bad days but that server was just plain rude. Will NEVER be going back.
author: Tony Moore

text:
I recently ordered a Happy Meal expecting it to include the advertised toy, but instead, I received a drawing book without any prior notice or explanation. There were no signs in the store indicating that the toys were out of stock, and the staff did not acknowledge the issue or offer an apology.

While I understand that inventory shortages can happen, it would have been reasonable for the staff to at least inform customers before ordering or express some understanding of the disappointment. Transparency and basic customer service would have made the situation much more acceptable.

I hope this feedback can help improve the experience for future customers.
author: Ning T

text: Congratulations to this McDonald's for showing me the most disastrous Big Mac in history! A sauce party? Yes, but not on my plate—it's all over the box and the burger shell. Clearly, the chef was working off the rule 'how much sauce does it take to ruin a burger.' Thank you for your 'thoughtful' service, showing me that a burger can indeed 'drink' sauce! Next time, could you provide a straw? Just in case I end up having to drink the sauce! If your goal was to make customers eat messily, well, congratulations, you’ve succeeded!
author: Forest Ji

text: Came here with my friend and she ordered a McMuffin, which she payed for on the kiosk and the kitchen refused to make it. When we inquired about the missing item at the counter the girl working there rolled her eyes and sent us away.  They also refused to turn on the outlets in the dining area even though im a paying customer, I’m sure the million dollar corporation can afford me charging my phone. . Not a good experience you’re better off going across the street to hungry jacks. PS no straws either

text:
I’m a regular here and I know they’re usually busy, but today’s experience was truly disappointing. I was really hungry, but halfway through my meal, I found that the chicken was still raw inside — something I’ve never experienced here before.
After reporting the issue, the response was just as unsatisfactory. Although they remade the dish, the manager handled it with a dismissive attitude and barely acknowledged the problem.
Really disappointed and won’t be coming back.
author: Joey Zou

text: I ordered a double cheeseburger at McDonald's Queen Street (restaurant 1514) on Wednesday 15 Dec 2021, at 15.10. The restaurant was not busy. Staff were standing around waiting for orders to be made. This is the quality and presentation of the burger given to me during a slow period. What has happened to presentation and standards? UPDATE: I visited this store a day or two later and ordered the same burger. The presentation was better this time around.
